newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Boral sees higher 2nd half profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Boral sees higher 2nd half profit.

text.p: Building products manufacturer Boral Ltd said the second half of the 1996/97 financial year to June 30 would be challenging but it expected profits to be above the level of the corresponding period in 1995/96.

In a statement accompanying the group's first half results, Boral Managing Director Tony Berg said: "There is no doubt now that housing starts have bottomed and we are expecting a modest recovery to commence soon."
"Consequently, the current half year will again be challenging but we expect management actions to deliver a profit above that of the corresponding period last year," he said.
Boral said improved demand for home building products in Australia was foreseen towards the end of the current half year after allowing for a lag between approvals and actual building.
Results from its construction materials division were expected to exceed the previous corresponding period, it said.
The steady performance of the energy group was expected to continue, Boral said.

The strong market conditions in the U.S. would be reflected in the full year results but the current half year would be impacted by Briar Gypsum, which was sold in December, being included for only one month.
Boral said its operations in Europe and Asia would face difficult market conditions.

Berg said margins had been squeezed even further in the first half as housing activity declined for the fourth consecutive half. As a result operating profit before tax and abnormal items declined by 13 percent to A$155.8 million.

"However, we are encouraged by the significant pickup in earnings," Berg said. "We have continued to focus the Group's activities on its core businesses, while, in tandem, we have taken many initiatives to cut costs from all our operations and make many other improvements."
